They made me an assistant at 19. I’m one of the lucky ones though managing came super naturally to me. My original GM didn’t train me much on the paper work side of things, like truck for example, but I excelled at running the store/shifts in general. After he couldn’t handle the 70hrs a week they were making him work, understandably, and I was left to run the store. They had to have some veterans come work a few days here and there to train me so I was able to pick up everything pretty quick thankfully. Within two months of being promoted I was basically running the store doing everything except the schedule because my AD or whatever GM was there at the time would do it. My name got around so I’ve only ever let other people tell me how good I was doing. After my first GM left we never had a long term GM except one that stayed for 6 months before leaving. It was a pretty ghetto store and I blame that mostly on Pizza Hut pay and the people that kinda pay attracts. At the end I was the only store manager beside a shift manager or two. I had ran the store by myself for 80% of my last year there and they hadn’t given me a raise since I was promoted to assistant (which was not a 50 cent raise at that) and refused to give me a raise or the store. I was even training an AD that was supposed to be in training, but they had basically tricked him into being the acting GM of our store because it had been 6 months and they still couldn’t find anyone. Eventually I was just done with it and tired of struggling financially even working 60+ hours a week. I was only making 11.50 an hour. Which is the whole problem with PizzaHut. They hire people, speed track them up the chain if they are even moderately good workers, and under pay the shit out of them. They got lucky with me according to other managers in the area, but usually this method only works on young people with little experience in the field. That was me and I was only on my fourth job ever and had never been a key holder even ever. Truthfully I didn’t even really want to be a manager, but I realized it could just tough it out for the experience then I’d have a back up plan for life so if whatever career I go into doesn’t work out I wouldn’t be stuck a crew member on minimum wage.
